Grab Doubles Down on Consumer Lending With Atome Deal — Interview
By Kimberley Kao
Grab Holdings is betting on consumer lending in Southeast Asia for growth, as the super app takes its acquisition spree to the region.
Its deal to acquire digital finance services platform Atome represents a multibillion dollar bet on distributing credit to millions of users across the region.
"We've added a new engine of growth for Grab's revenue and earnings," said Alex Hungate, Grab's president and chief operating officer, in an interview.
Currently, only 1% of Grab's 138 million annual transacting user base have taken out a loan through its existing financial products, Hungate said.
"Together with Atome, since they're the market leader in the consumer credit category, we intend to penetrate from 1% to 10% over time," he said.
Atome operates in Singapore, Malaysia, the Philippines, Indonesia and Thailand, and serves 25 million cumulative transacted users.

The deal values Atome at up to $4.5 billion under a performance-based payout structure. Grab is purchasing an initial 60% stake entirely in cash for $1.49 billion, with the remaining 40% tied to earnings and revenue targets about two years after the completion of the first transaction.
The deal prompted Grab to raise its 2028 adjusted Ebitda target to $1.7 billion from $1.5 billion, and its compound annual revenue growth rate to 30% from 20% for the 2025 to 2028 period.

Grab has increasingly turned to acquisitions to support its growth this year. It bought U.S.-based Stash Financial at an enterprise value of $425 million and agreed to buy Foodpanda's Taiwan operations from Delivery Hero for $600 million.
Still, any acquisitions Grab does will remain "disciplined" and "must be an extraordinarily good fit with our strategy," Hungate said.

"[Atome's] valuation leaves little room for error," Maybank Research analyst Hussaini Saifee said in a note. The "key execution test" is whether the two businesses can work together and generate enough shared value that will justify the capital spent by Grab, he said.

While the acquisition could expand Grab's addressable market and support stronger growth beyond 2028, "it lowers the near-term earnings flow-through from Atome, Superbank and Foodpanda Taiwan, and raises the execution bar for achieving the upgraded [earnings] target," Saifee said, referring to investments Grab has announced this year.
